claim: Approximately three-quarters of US iPhone sales go through mobile carriers, giving carrier store staff influence over both model choice and platform choice.
stance_target: Ecosystem lock-in is structural, not switching-cost/contractual inertia
quoted_support: With about three-quarters of US iPhone sales going through carriers, Apple relies heavily on AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, and the rest for initial sales and follow-up service. Carriers control the sales transaction, where store staff can influence choice of model, and even whether a customer remains with iPhone or switches to Android.

claim: iOS loyalty declines measurably among iPhone owners who switch mobile carriers, compared to iPhone owners who keep the same carrier.
stance_target: Ecosystem lock-in is structural, not switching-cost/contractual inertia
scope_conditions: US, CIRP quarterly buyer survey, all smartphone buyers
quoted_support: Loyalty to iOS declines when an iPhone owner moves to a new mobile phone company. ... The loyalty rate was lower for iPhone users who changed mobile carriers.

claim: About one-quarter of all smartphone buyers (across brands) switch mobile carriers when buying a new phone, with a slightly higher carrier-switching rate among Android buyers than iOS buyers.
stance_target: Carrier churn as a contributing mechanism to platform switching
scope_conditions: US, CIRP quarterly mobile phone buyer survey (all brands)
quoted_support: about one-quarter of buyers switch mobile carriers when they buy a new smartphone, with a slightly higher percentage of Android users than iOS users switching.

claim: Overall iPhone loyalty rate was 89% for the twelve-month period ending June 2025, per CIRP's mobile phone buyer survey.
stance_target: Ecosystem lock-in is structural (high headline loyalty)
quoted_support: For the twelve-month period ending in June 2025, iPhone had a loyalty rate of 89% (Chart 1).
